codegen_equivalence.method: g++ -m32 -std=c++17 -O2 -c, then objdump -d of the emitted .text body, compared against the 52 original bytes
codegen_equivalence.O2: Both comparison immediates (cmp $0xeec58382 / cmp $0xeef3af8c), both displacements (lea 0x4(%ecx) / lea 0xc(%ecx)), the shared null materialisation (xor %eax,%eax) and the callee-cleanup form (ret $0x4 on all three exits) are all present. Not byte-identical: the compiler adds a PIC thunk prologue for the external call, lowers the tail jump to call/ret, and reassociates the two LEA+RET pairs into one shared ADD/LEA block. The 0x009817d2 store is eliminated, which is correct -- it is a no-op on the value.
codegen_equivalence.O0: Closer in shape but not in structure: at -O0 the two named helpers (offset_address, null_word) are not inlined, so the emitted body contains four real CALL instructions where the original body contains none. The single callee-cleaned ret $0x4, both immediates, both displacements and both null tests are still present. Byte correspondence is therefore NOT claimed at -O0, and this package does not claim it.

Nothing this package writes can move it: the abstention is a property of the evidence pack, and the pack is out of bounds. This package followed the persisted __thiscall claim anyway and documented which half of the convention the machine proves (4-byte callee cleanup, SUPPORTED) and which half it does not (the receiver, abstained).
expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS, expected. The xref export and the complete 17-instruction listing independently name the same single direct transfer target, 0x00951240, reached by a jump. The register-agnostic arm needs a listing with no memory operand through ANY register, and this listing has two: MOV EAX,[ESP + 0x4] at 0x009817c0 and MOV [ESP + 0x4],EAX at 0x009817d2. The helper's own docstring says over-reporting is the safe direction and that a false hit costs the pass, so [ESP + 0x4] takes the body out of that arm by design. The only way this package could move the check off NOT_AVAILABLE is by declaring a field offset in the source, which would land it on the reconstruction-declared WARN arm instead -- still not a pass, and it would mean asserting a member layout that no record for this target supports. That trade was declined. NOT_AVAILABLE is the accurate answer: the machine evidence cannot adjudicate this body in either direction.

contradictions.summary: The queue record and the Spore-ModAPI import both name this address UTFWin::ScrollbarDrawable::SetImage. The body is not a setter: it takes one 32-bit comparison key and a receiver address, returns the address of one of the receiver's words or null, writes nothing, never dereferences the receiver, and is never passed an image pointer. A SetImage that stored an image into a scrollbar would have to write through the receiver. No reading of these 17 instructions is a setter.
contradictions.consequence: The reconstruction models the observed behaviour and keeps the record's last name component inside the entry symbol only because the validator binds a source span by matching it. No semantic claim is made that this function is a SetImage, and the .cpp header block says so in terms.

contradictions.summary: The imported prototype is void UTFWin::ScrollbarDrawable::SetImage(IScrollbarDrawable *this, int index, Image *pImage) with ghidra_parameter_count 3. Two ordinary stack arguments under a callee-cleaned convention would require RET 0x8, but all three exits of the body are RET 0x4 and the body reads only entry_ESP+0x4. The declared void return is contradicted by EAX being written with an address on every path. The machine contract is a one-stack-word callee returning a pointer in EAX. The imported prototype is rejected and not used.

The live decompilation renders the argument as IScrollbarDrawable *this, compares THAT pointer against 0xeec58382 and 0xeef3af8c, declares the result void, and discards the EAX results of both LEAs and of the XOR -- so the three return paths the body actually implements are all rendered as a bare return. The decompiler is mis-typing a uint32 key as the receiver pointer because the imported prototype forces a receiver-typed first parameter. The reconstruction is based on the disassembly and on the raw bytes, never on that rendering, and the .cpp says so.

The ghidra_function record lists four xrefs to this address (01441a50, 01444880, 00969b43, 00969b53) and the briefing's dependency export reports the out-edge 0x009817d6 -> 0x00951240 as a direct-call. All of these are references rather than calls: 01441a50 and 01444880 are data-segment vtable slots, and 0x00969b43 and 0x00969b53 are the JMP operands of the two this-adjusting thunks (0x00969b40 is SUB ECX,0x4 / JMP 0x009817c0; 0x00969b50 is SUB ECX,0xc / JMP 0x009817c0). fan_in is 0 and callers is empty, so the function has no direct caller at all: it is reached only by virtual dispatch and by those two thunks.

The persisted abi record gives return_type 'void*'. The machine-derived record gives return_semantics 'integral_in_EAX'. Both agree EAX is written on every path and that the word is 4 bytes wide. Every value EAX can hold on this body is an address -- the receiver, the receiver plus a proven displacement, or zero -- which is what makes void* defensible and is the spelling the package uses. The derived record's 'integral' classification is not refuted by anything in this body, and the conflict is not resolved here.
contradictions.consequence: RETURN SEMANTICS passes because the declared text matches the persisted record's token. That is a text match, not a resolution of the category question, and it should not be read as one.

unresolved_questions: What generates the four constants 0x6ec58382, 0xeef3af8c, 0xee3f516e and 0x6ec581fd? They are used only as equality keys in these two bodies. Whether they are hashes of type names, field names or something else is not observable here, and this package therefore does not call the argument a hash in its own types even though the record does.

What are the declared names and types of the words at +0x00, +0x04 and +0x0c of the receiver? The offsets are proven by the LEAs and the ADD; nothing in either body dereferences a typed field, so no name or type is recoverable from this target alone.

Which C++ class owns this address, and which interface is its vtable slot a member of? SporeApp.exe carries no MSVC RTTI, so class identity cannot be read from the binary. The record's vtable list is a transitive classifier association and was deliberately not used to name a class.

Why does the 0x6ec581fd arm of 0x00951240 return the receiver with no null guard, while every other arm in both bodies is guarded? The asymmetry is observed, reproduced in the test, and not explained: whether it is intentional in the original source or an artefact of how the resolver was generated is not determinable from the machine.

Is the MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x4],EAX at 0x009817d2 an artefact of the original build's tail-call lowering, or an explicit argument write in the source? It is a no-op on the value either way, and the test cannot observe it -- mutation M10 confirms that removing it leaves the test green. The model states it rather than assuming it away, and that limit is stated in the test as well.

Are the two this-adjusting thunks 0x00969b40 and 0x00969b50 members of the same interface as this slot, and is the base class boundary at 0x009817c0 or 0x009817b0? The thunks' SUB ECX displacements match this body's two LEA displacements exactly, which is suggestive, but no slot index is claimed for either thunk's own table.

Is the base of the vtable containing 0x00951240 identifiable, and does it share an interface with the tables that contain this target? Only the single pointer occurrence is established; no slot index is claimed for it.
